title: TMP Camera Surveillance Next 2.20.70
summary: Reject false Reolink camera matches from TCP 8443+9000 and prevent old discovery flags persisting.
changes: Do not identify Reolink by an open 9000 vendor port and a generic HTTPS port alone
Reevaluate port-based proof on every final discovery policy application
Remove old invalid Reolink manufacturer labels and stale manually scanned entries
Preserve verified ONVIF and RTSP/RTMP camera discovery
Keep full go2rtc race protection, motion, recording and HLS compatibility
name: TMP Camera Surveillance Next v2.20.70
description: Correct vendor inference and final camera discovery classification; reset stale manual scan results.
releaseNotes: Compatible from 2.20.32. TCP 9000 + generic HTTPS is no longer enough to identify a Reolink camera. RTSP, RTMP or explicit ONVIF/vendor API evidence remains eligible. Current scan recomputes port signature, stale scan flags are discarded, and each new manual scan resets results. Preserves recordings, cameras and .env.
